name: ZIM@SBB
tagline: A white-label build of the ZIM eSIM app for Swiss Federal Railways, shipped as its own app in four languages.

overview.text: ZIM@SBB is a white-label build of the ZIM eSIM app for Swiss Federal Railways (SBB), shipped as its own app.
It provides eSIM connectivity in four languages, using i18next and Locize.
It runs on ZIM's shared multi-tenant platform, which, as of the September 2026 CV, served 4 production brands and 11 app identities on shared infrastructure.

responsibilities.text: Delivered the ZIM@SBB integration with Swiss Federal Railways.

Tested the full journey on physical iPhones and Android phones, because eSIMs cannot be installed on a simulator. The tests covered Cognito sign-in, expired sessions, permission prompts granted and denied, and buying and installing an eSIM on weak or no signal.

Identified both translation defects during pre-release testing: the missing translation keys and the truncated button on smaller iPhones. The records don't say who wrote the key-comparison script or who implemented the fixes.
Worked closely with the product team, reviewing builds together before each release to get every string, asset and flow right in all four languages.

overview.text: ZIM@SBB shares the core application and backend with the other ZIM brands. Partner-specific behaviour is kept in configuration rather than in the core.
Translations are managed with i18next in the app and Locize as the translation management service.

challenges.title: Multi-tenancy without forks
challenges.problem: SBB needed its own branded app on the same platform as ZIM's other brands, and each new partner risked a fork of the codebase.
approach: Keep partner-specific behaviour in configuration rather than the core.
challenges.outcome: A new partner is a configuration change, not a fork. As of the September 2026 CV, the platform ran 4 brands and 11 app identities.

challenges.title: Catching translation defects before release
challenges.problem: AI first-pass translations dropped two Italian keys and truncated a button on smaller iPhones.
approach: A key-comparison script to find translation keys missing in any language (who wrote it isn't recorded).
On-device checks to catch layout problems such as truncated text.
challenges.outcome: During pre-release testing, Alex identified both defects, and both were fixed before release.

challenges.title: Testing an eSIM journey that cannot run in a simulator
challenges.problem: eSIMs cannot be installed on a simulator, and travellers often buy and install them on weak or no signal.
approach: End-to-end testing on physical iPhones and Android phones.
Covered sign-in, expired sessions, permission prompts granted and denied, and purchase and installation on poor connectivity.

decisions.title: Partner behaviour in configuration, not in the core
decisions.decision: SBB-specific behaviour lives in configuration on the shared platform rather than in a separate codebase.
decisions.rationale: Adding the next partner is then a configuration change rather than a fork.

lessons.text: The hard part of white-labelling is not the theming but keeping partner-specific behaviour out of the core.
AI-generated translations need mechanical checks (key comparison) and on-device review; they can silently drop keys or break layouts.

limitations.text: This is employer-owned work. The source code is private, so details here come from Alex's CV and notes.
